gsmConnectionStatusReason.title: gsmConnectionStatusReason
gsmConnectionStatusReason.description:
GSM connection status reason
SIM_MISSING - Indicates that the SIM card is not detected or missing. This could be due to the SIM card not being inserted correctly, a faulty SIM card, or a SIM card that is not compatible with the modem
SIM_PIN_MISSING - Indicates that a PIN is required to unlock the SIM card, but it has not been provided or entered incorrectly. The modem is unable to establish a connection until the correct PIN is entered
SIM_PUK_REQUIRED - Indicates that the SIM card is locked due to too many incorrect PIN entries, and a Personal Unlocking Key (PUK) is required to unlock it. The modem cannot establish a connection until the correct PUK is entered
HARDWARE_FAILURE - Indicates a hardware failure or issue with the modem itself. This could be due to a malfunctioning modem, improper connections, or other hardware-related problems
NO_NETWORK_SERVICE - Indicates that the modem is unable to find or connect to a network service. This could be due to factors such as weak signal strength, network coverage issues, or configuration problems
SIM_LOCKED - Indicates that the SIM card is locked to a specific network and cannot be used with the current modem. Unlocking the SIM card or using a SIM card from the correct network may resolve this issue
UNKNOWN - Indicates a non-standard value for connection status reason, which may indicate the modem is not completely started

get.description:
This will trigger retrieval if necessary (MVA records are not yet synched).
    The retrieval (records synch) operation is done asynchronously.

    Before exporting the records, this endpoint must be called to ensure
    that all records have been synched (and thus are ready for export).

    As the synching of the records might take a while, after calling this
    you can check the status of the synch with the dedicated endpoint.

    Args:
        serialNumber: the serial number of the wallbox we want to export the records for
        type: the type of mva record (MEASUREMENT or LOG)
        list: optional list of specific records to retrieve. Format is: 1,3,5-8,20,50-101.
            Not specifying the list will retrieve all records of given type.

    Return:
        MvaResponse holding the process information
        ResponseMessage indicating any failure

    Example:
        Retrieve all LOG records
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/mvas/synch/1234678/LOG

        Retrieve records 1 and 5 through 10
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/mvas/synch/12345678/LOG?list=1,5-10

        Retrieve all MEASUREMENT records
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/mvas/synch/12345678/MEASUREMENT?list=1,5-10

get.description:
Args:
        TokenQuery: criteria that matches the returned Tokens
    Returns:
        list json list of Token.
            Note that the result is automatically limited to 1024 entries.
        responseMessage indicating the details of failure

    Example:
        Get max 1024 tokens (ordered by ascending id)
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/

        Get next 10 tokens starting from the 5th result of all tokens in descending order by their name.
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/?offset=5&limit=10&orderField=NAME&orderDir=DESC'

        Get latest 10 rfids ordered by last used date descending that are ACCEPTED
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/?offset=0&limit=10&orderField=USED_DATE&orderDir=DESC&filters=STATUS=ACCEPTED'

        Find token by name
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/?offset=0&limit=1&filters=NAME=Card1'

        Get all rfids used in the given interval: use one of: '-gt' '-gte' '-lt' '-lte' '-eq' after the field name
        Notice the same filter criteria twice:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/?filters=USED_DATE-gte=1639569600&filters=USED_DATE-lte=1639584118101'
        Same action as above but using some UTC formatted dates (url encoded of 15-12-2021 14:00:00 to 15-12-2021 18:01:58):
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/rfids/?filters=USED_DATE-gte=15-12-2021%2014%3A00%3A00&filters=USED_DATE-lte=15-12-2021%2018%3A01%3A58'

    Returns:

            Note that the result is automatically limited to 200 entries.

    Example:
        Get the latest 200 sessions (ordered by descending session start date)
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/

        Get the next 10 sessions starting from the 5th result of all sessions in descending order by their session start date.
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?offset=5&limit=10&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC'

        Get the latest 10 sessions ordered by session start date descending that belong to the Wallbox with serial number 16350815
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?offset=0&limit=10&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC&filters=SOCKET_SERIAL_NUMBER=16350815'

        Find the latest Session authorized with a specific Token
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?offset=0&limit=1&orderField=SESSION_START_DATE&orderDir=DESC&filters=CHARGING_TOKEN_ID=4444444'

        Get all sessions in the given interval (intrinsec comparator for SESSION_START_DATE is '-gte' and for SESSION_END_DATE is '-lte')
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE=1639569600000&filters=SESSION_END_DATE=1639584118101'
        Same action as above but using some UTC formatted dates (url encoded of 15-12-2021 14:00:00 to 15-12-2021 18:01:58):
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE=15-12-2021%2014%3A00%3A00&filters=SESSION_END_DATE=15-12-2021%2018%3A01%3A58'

        Use comparators for fields: use one of: '-gt' '-gte' '-lt' '-lte' '-eq' after the field name
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE-gt=1639569600000&filters=SESSION_END_DATE-lte=1639584118101'

        Use multiple filter occurrences:
        curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --insecure 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/sessions/?filters=SESSION_START_DATE-gt=1639569600&filters=SESSION_START_DATE-lt=1639584118101'

        Use multiple filter values (comma separated); translates into an OR query. Works with a limited subset of filters:

post.description:
This will trigger automatic retrieval and installation of a .raucb file indicated
    at a given location (ftp, http/https).
    The status of the download and installation can be checked with /request/status endpoint.

    Args:
        location      : is mandatory and has to point to the given rauc bundle (ftp/http/https sources).
        retrieveDate  : unix time - can be in the future. If it is in the past, retrieval starts immediately.
        installDate   : unix time - must be after retrieve date. If retrieve has not yet finished,
                            install will run immediately after retrieve finishes.
        retries       : number of retries to try and retrieve the rauc bundle. Consider using a large number over a bad network.
        retryInterval : time between retries (sec)
    Only for signed updates:
        signingCertificate  : the public certificate used for signing the rauc bundle update (.pem format). To set the
                                  certification as .json payload inside a string, it must be escaped.
        signature           : the signature of the rauc bundle update

    Return:
        ResponseMessage indicating the result of the operation

    Example:
    Regular update:
        curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -X POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/updates/request -d'{ "location" : "http://127.0.0.1/p40-system.raucb", "retrieveDate" : 1641566534, "installDate" : 1641566534, "retries" : 10, "retryInterval" : 30}'
    Signed update:
        curl -v --header "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" --header "Content-Type: application/json" --request POST --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/v2/updates/request --data-raw '{ "location" : "http://127.0.0.1/p40-system.raucb" , "retrieveDate" : 1641566534, "installDate" : 1641566534, "retries" : 10, "retryInterval" : 30, "signature" : "'...'", "signingCertificate" : "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- ... -----END CERTIFICATE-----"}'

The RESTAPI version scheme has format Major.Minor.Patch (for example, 1.0.0)
    Major versions have breaking changes in them and aren't backward compatible.
        They're also indicated in the path (/v1 for 1.X.Y or /v2 for 2.X.Y).
    Minor versions are backward compatible through the Major version. (1.2.0 will support all functions of 1.0.0).
        Note that some new fields could be added in a Minor version, but no fields are deleted or renamed.
    Patch versions only solve very specific problems and shouldn't break the Minor version formatting.
        Expect this for non-functional changes (backend changes).

    Returns:

    Example:
        curl --insecure https://127.0.0.1:8443/version
